en: Udāna 7.4 The Second Discourse on Beings.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now at that time, the people of Sāvatthī for the most part were attached to sensual pleasures—infatuated, greedy, fettered, infatuated, and clinging; blinded, utterly obsessed, they lived amidst sensual pleasures.
Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.
The Blessed One saw those people in Sāvatthī who, for the most part, were dwelling amidst sensual pleasures—attached, greedy, fettered, infatuated, obsessed, blinded, and possessed by them.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Blinded by sensual pleasure, shrouded by a net...”
Covered by the veil of craving,
bound by the kinsman of negligence,
they are like fish at the mouth of a net.
They follow after aging and death,
just as a suckling calf follows its mother.
